column4: Rule
User-exits, enhancements, and BADIs must be implemented by SAP Operation.
Standard modifications (with modification key) must be implemented by SAP Operation.
Standard indexes must be implemented by SAP Operation.
BADI must be evaluated first as the integration option.
If no suitable BADI exists, a customer exit must be evaluated next.
If no BADI or customer exit exists, a standard include program must be evaluated for enhancement.
Events (based on modification object technology) must be evaluated as the last option.
Database COMMIT must not execute in the middle of a SAP standard transaction (e.g., user exit, enhancement).
Data in SAP standard tables must not manipulated directly in custom programs.
Standard functions, BAPIs, or data classes should be used to create, update, or delete standard SAP data.
Direct database operations (UPDATE, DELETE, INSERT, MODIFY) should not be performed on SAP standard tables or tables from packages ZPR21 / ZZB160.
When an exception is required, it must be logged in table ZDCZZT94 and handled by SAP Operation.
Text enhancements must not be used.
FIELD-EXIT must not be used.
When a project uses a BADI, its specific entry must be created in ZDCZZT20 before coding.
Each project must implement its logic in its own specific class.
Required check parameters must be evaluated at the beginning of each BADI method.
Only BADI methods with significant parameters should be used.
Only one implementation per Business Add-In must be activated at the same time.
If the BADI does not provide the exception parameter CANCEL, include ZPCZZI21 must be used.
For each new functionality requested by a project, the ABAP code must be written in a project-specific class.
A new project-specific class Z<MYCLASS> must be created and registered in table ZDCZZT20.
Class Z<MYCLASS> must be created using transaction SE24.
The project-specific class Z<MYCLASS> must be automatically called via include ZPCZZI20 based on the entry in ZDCZZT20.
